To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytotoxic effects on HeLa cells of nemorosones and clusianones are similar and that the cytotoxicity is enantiospecific.
all four enantiopure nemorosone analogs are active in the HeLa cell screen.

all the enantiomers of the PPAPs tested were equally cytotoxic against HeLa, MIA-PaCA-2, and MCF7 cell lines, and that the PPAPs were less cytotoxic against HeLA cells than against MCF7 and MIA-PaC-2 cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the total synthesis of polyprenyl acylphlorogluconol derivatives and the evaluation of their cytotoxicity.
the development of a synthetic route to the nemorosone skeleton, the synthesis of the enantiomeric pair of the natural product, and the evaluation of these enantiomers as cytotoxic agents.

the development of new synthetic methods for the preparation of polyprenyl acylphloro-glu-cinol natural products and analogues, and the study of the structure-activity relationships of these natural products and analogs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytotoxic effects observed are not due to the enantioselective properties of the PPAPs, but rather due to the presence of a polyprenyl group.
the cytotoxicity of these compounds is not dependent on the stereochemistry of the polyprenyl side chain, the position of the acyl side chain, or the stereochemistry of that side chain.
nemorosone is not the most potent PPAP, and that the enantiomeric pairs of PPAPs, nemorosone, and clusianones are all very similar in cytotoxic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PPAPs, regardless of their absolute configuration or regiochemistry, are potent inhibitors of cell growth, and that the enantiomeric pair of each PPAP has essentially identical activity.
the cytotoxic effects are due to the polyprenyl chain and not the acylphloroglocinol core.
the PPAPs are not very cytotoxic, even in the enantiopure forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytotoxic effects are independent of the stereochemical configuration of the PPAPs, and that the presence or absence of an additional prenyl chain at the 3-position does not seem to be important.
the stereochemistry of the PPAPs is not critical in determining cytotoxicity.
the cytotoxicity of these compounds does not seem to depend on the chirality of the polyprenyl chain, nor on the regiochemistry of the acylphlorogluinol moiety.
